category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your coworker from Columbus says the Big Ten is actually better now, and points at recent playoff results. Respond as an SEC fan. Hold the line.
response:
Oh, here we go. Let me guess — you've got your Michigan 2023 and Ohio State 2024 talking points loaded up like it erases twenty years of history. Cute.

Look, I'll give you this: the Big Ten has had a nice little moment. Congrats. Two titles. You know what we call two titles down here? *A slow stretch.* The SEC won 13 of 17 national championships from 2006 to 2022. Alabama alone has more titles this century than your entire conference. That's not a rivalry, that's a landlord-tenant relationship.

And let's talk about *how* those recent Big Ten titles happened. Michigan beat an Alabama team in Nick Saban's last season on a walk-off in overtime — one play from a different conversation. And Ohio State's run? They lost to *Michigan* at home as three-touchdown favorites, backed into the playoff, and got hot. Respect the run, but don't act like that's sustained dominance. That's catching lightning.

Meanwhile, look at the depth. NFL Draft picks? SEC. Recruiting rankings? SEC, top to bottom. Your conference has like three real programs and then a bunch of teams that treat 7-5 like a parade-worthy season. Our *middle class* — your Ole Misses, your Tennessees — would be contending in the Big Ten every year.

You added Oregon, Washington, and USC just to keep up. You had to annex the entire Pacific coast to compete. We just... kept being the SEC.

So enjoy the moment, Columbus. Take pictures. Because the pendulum always swings back, and when it does, it's going to swing back wearing crimson, orange, or purple and gold.

It just means more. Always has. 🏈
